    Lemma 2.9 for an arbitrary finite-dimensional algebra #

    lem:projective-evaluation-criterion (graded-category.tex): "Let Λ be a finite-dimensional algebra over any field, let e be an idempotent, and put Λ_e = eΛe. Assume Hom_Λ(T, Λ) = Ext¹_Λ(T, Λ) = 0 whenever Te = 0. Then P ↦ Pe is fully faithful on proj Λ. If gl.dim Λ ≤ 2 and every finite-dimensional injective Λ_e-module is Qe for some projective Λ-module Q, this functor is an equivalence proj Λ ≃ mod Λ_e. In particular, Λ_e is representation-finite. It suffices to check the two vanishings on the simple Λ-modules killed by e."

    Conventions. The manuscript's right Λ-modules are the left modules over R = Λᵐᵒᵖ, and Me is ε M for ε = op e; so we work with left modules over an arbitrary finite-dimensional algebra R and an idempotent ε. Λ_e is Mathlib's corner ring hε.Corner (ε R ε, with unit ε), and ε M is a Λ_e-module (EP); evaluation is EPmap. Ext¹_R(T, Q) = 0 is taken in Yoneda form: every extension 0 → Q → E → T → 0 splits (ExtVan). gl.dim R ≤ 2 is used, as in the proof, through "a second syzygy is projective": the kernel of a map between finitely generated projectives is projective.

    The proof is the source's, without tensor products (as in ProjectiveEvaluation.lean): a map g : εM → εQ is defined on the submodule generated by εM by ∑ λ_i m_i ↦ ∑ λ_i g(m_i), well defined because the discrepancy is a submodule of Q killed by ε; it extends to M because M / R εM is killed by ε (Ext¹); injectivity is the Hom-vanishing for M / R εM.
